editionStmt.p: The five Ethiopian manuscripts belonging to the Ferdinando Martini collection at the Forteguerriana Library in Pistoia were digitized in May–June 2018 by Antonella Brita, Karsten Helmholz, and Susanne Hummel, as part of a cooperative project for the documentation and digitization of Ethiopian manuscript collections in Italian libraries—including the non-invasive sampling of materials for scientific analysis—directed by Alessandro Bausi (University of Hamburg) and coordinated by Antonella Brita (University of Hamburg and, since 2021, the University of Florence). The project was conducted under the auspices of the Hiob Ludolf Centre for Ethiopian and Eritrean Studies (HLCEES) and the Centre for the Study of Manuscript Cultures (CSMC) at the University of Hamburg. This initiative was funded by the Centre for the Study of Manuscript Cultures (CSMC); by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) through the project (TP C05) ‘“Parchment Saints” – The Making of Ethiopian Hagiographic Manuscripts: Matter and Devotion in Manuscript Practices of Medieval and Pre-Modern Ethiopia’—part of the cooperative research unit (Sonderforschungsbereich) 950 ‘Manuskriptkulturen in Asien, Afrika und Europa’ at the University of Hamburg (2015–2019); and by the European Research Council under the European Union’s Seventh Framework Programme (FP7/2007–2013) IDEAS, Advanced Grant Agreement No. 338756, for the project ‘TraCES – From Translation to Creation: Changes in Ethiopic Style and Lexicon from Late Antiquity to the Middle Ages’ at the University of Hamburg (2014–2019). The initial cataloguing was carried out for the CaNaMEI project by Massimo Villa (philological part) and Gioia Bottari (codicological part), University of Naples L'Orientale, and converted to the Bm format (see Revision history).

handNote.seg: Several lines of the incipits of the texts, included subsections; divine names; elements of the punctuation, text dividers, and numerals

decoNote.desc: Drawing of the cardinal points, consisting of three concentric circles in red ink. The circular area between the two outer circles is divided internally into eight sections, labelled with the names of the eight cardinal directions.

Drawing of the cardinal points and the Ethiopian regions, consisting of three concentric circles in red ink. The circular area between the two outer circles is divided internally into twelve sections, labelled with the name of twelve Ethiopian regions. The circular area between the two inner circles is divided internally into eight sections, labelled with the names of the eight cardinal directions. A central rectangle is labelled ‘ʾAksum’.

list.item: Note in crude hand, which is hardly legible, representing possibly a supplication, a magic prayer or an ownership note. binding.decoNote: Two wooden boards covered with reddish-brown leather. Both boards have textile inlays. Four sewing stations.
The front, back and spine cover are decorated with blind-tooled ornament.
Two pairs of sewing stations. Two Z-twisted threads (each thread is S-twisted) of animal origin.. Sewing pattern: Bozzacchi A2.
The maḫdär consists of two cases, one inside the other. Material: yellow-brownish leather. Size: 275 x 252 x 62 mm Thickness of the leather: ca. 2.15–2.75 mm
